title: Food Science — Heat Transfer and Functional Properties

flashcard_questions.a: Conduction (direct contact through solids), convection (circular currents in liquids/gases), and radiation (infrared waves without contact).
flashcard_questions.q: What are the three methods of heat transfer in cooking?

flashcard_questions.a: The process by which starch granules absorb water and swell when heated, eventually bursting to thicken a liquid into a gel-like consistency.
Denaturation (unwinding of protein molecules), coagulation (setting into a solid), gluten formation (elastic dough), and foam formation (trapping air when whisked).
flashcard_questions.q: Name the four functional properties of protein.

flashcard_questions.a: Dextrinisation is the browning of starch by dry heat (e.g. toast). Caramelisation is the browning of sugar when heated above its melting point (e.g. crème brûlée).
flashcard_questions.q: What is the difference between dextrinisation and caramelisation?
